build_note: Installed from the pinned pure-Python py3-none-any wheel by hash; the image checks that the wheel sqlglot/ package is byte-identical to the pinned sdist, that sqlglot/parser.py, sqlglot/tokens.py and the MIT LICENSE match recorded SHA-256 values, that there are no unconditional runtime dependencies, and that the optional sqlglotc and sqlglotrs accelerators are absent, so the pure-Python tokenizer and parser run.
dependencies_note: atheris 3.1.0 is the in-process fuzz bridge only; sqlglot has no runtime dependencies.
parser_family: sqlglot pure-Python tokenizer (sqlglot/tokens.py, tokenizer_core.py) and recursive-descent parser (sqlglot/parser.py, sqlglot/parsers) building an Expression tree; independent of sqlparse, libpg_query and sqlparser-rs
dialect: sqlglot default dialect (read=None), the dialect-agnostic base Dialect
api: sqlglot.parse(local SQL text decoded from UTF-8 bytes, read=None) -> list of Expression trees; the harness walks exp.Select, exp.Insert, exp.Schema, exp.Values, exp.Table, exp.Func and exp.Literal nodes
coverage: Python line tracing of the sqlglot package source during valid-control replay; Atheris import instrumentation for the byte-input bridge
scope: One SQL statement from local text via sqlglot.parse with the default dialect; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls only, each matching the hand-written oracle summary. Dialect-specific syntax, error recovery levels and the optional compiled accelerators are untested.
